ActionType.description: Canonical action taxonomy for BH audit events. OVERRIDE records a human interrupting, cancelling, or reversing an agent action or session.

OutcomeStatus.description: Terminal outcome classification for an audited action.

DataClassification.description: Regulatory classification of the data touched by the action.

SubjectType.description: Identity class. 'human': an authenticated human user. 'service': deterministic code under its own service identity. 'agent': a non-deterministic AI actor operating under delegated human authority.

DelegationType.description: Human-oversight state at the time of an agent action. 'supervised': human actively observing, can intervene in real time. 'autonomous': agent acts without real-time human observation. 'scheduled': agent launched by a timer or trigger with no human present at execution.

AgentInterface.description: Interaction surface used by the agent. Determines risk class and available enforcement points.

AttributionLevel.description: How the event's attribution was established. 'verified': derived from a token whose issuer asserted the identities; not forgeable by the agent. 'bound': operator configuration maps a credential or session to an authorizing identity; this is the operator's assertion and is not proof of a human's involvement in this call. 'asserted': supplied by the agent in the call itself; forgeable by the agent. 'unattributed': an agent was involved and no authorizing human could be named; no delegation block is present. The levels are totally ordered, weakest to strongest: unattributed < asserted < bound < verified. Compare on position in that sequence, never on the serialized string (RFC 0003 section 4.4).

schema_version.description: Schema version for this audit event.

event_id.description: Globally unique UUID identifier for this audit event.

timestamp.description: UTC timestamp when the audited action occurred.

correlation.description: Identifiers used to correlate events across services. At least one ID required if present.

subject_type.description: The authenticating identity: the identity whose credentials were presented to the target system.

owner_org_id.description: Organization that owns the resource being accessed. Enables cross-org access detection.

roles.description: Optional roles at time of access.

method.description: Forensic detail on the mechanism behind the level, such as the credential type that carried the identities or the resolution paths that were attempted. Open vocabulary. Consumers reason over level, not method.

attribution.description: Optional top-level object stating how this event's attribution was established. Required whenever delegation is present, with level verified, bound, or asserted. With level 'unattributed' it records that an agent was involved and no authorizing human could be named, and delegation is then forbidden. When both attribution and delegation are absent, the event asserts that no agent was involved.

subject_type.description: Acting identity is always an agent; human-proxy delegation is deferred to a future version.

agent.description: Agent descriptor. No field may carry free-text prompt or configuration content.

subject_type.description: Authorizing identity is always a human. An agent cannot authorize. For sub-agent chains this is always the root human.

agent_session_id.description: Correlates every action to its session lifecycle events.

chain_depth.description: Depth 1 is an agent delegated directly by the authorizing human; depth 2 is a sub-agent spawned by a depth-1 agent.

parent_agent_session_id.description: Session ID of the parent agent for sub-agent chains. Present iff chain_depth >= 2.

delegation.description: Optional top-level object. Its presence asserts the action was agent-mediated and requires an attribution block stating how the block is known. Its absence asserts a direct, non-delegated action, unless attribution.level is 'unattributed'.

phi_touched.description: True if the action touches regulated PHI (behavioral health context).

type.description: E.g., Patient, Note, Encounter, Appointment, Program, AgentSession.

patient_id.description: Patient identifier if applicable. Recommended for PHI-touching actions.

error_message.description: Sanitized error message. Must not contain PHI.

outcome.description: DENIED indicates the system correctly refused access (not an error). FAILURE indicates an operational error. Both FAILURE and DENIED require error_type. error_message is optional on DENIED.

hash_alg.description: Hash algorithm used for tamper-evident chaining.

metadata.description: Optional safe metadata. Values must be scalar (no nested objects or arrays). Must not include raw PHI. Prompts, model outputs, screenshots, and reasoning traces are forbidden by structure: store such artifacts in a separately access-controlled store and reference them via an opaque identifier.

allOf.$comment: RFC 0003 R1. A delegation block must state how it is known, and cannot claim to be unattributed.
RFC 0003 R2. Level unattributed asserts there is no delegation block to describe.
RFC 0003 R3. A level other than unattributed describes a delegation block, so one must exist.
RFC 0003 R4, amended from 2.0. An agent authenticating identity is explained either by a delegation block or by an explicit unattributed level. Silence remains invalid.
RFC 0001 rule 3, amended by RFC 0003 to also forbid attribution. An override is a named human interrupting an agent session, so there is no agent attribution to state.
